agent_guide.title: Use YOLOZU with an LLM or agent
agent_guide.summary: Use YOLOZU when you need to validate existing vision predictions, evaluate them against labels, or inspect bounded local MCP capabilities.
use_when: Check a predictions JSON against the predictions interface contract before evaluation.
Evaluate existing detections against a labeled dataset with a fixed protocol and inspect the resulting evidence.
Integrate the typed Python API or discover local MCP tools and their input schemas before invoking them.
not_for: Do not infer model quality from a synthetic proof or a successful dry run. Real COCO metrics require the coco extra and labeled inputs.
Do not treat registered MCP tools as guaranteed execution. Runtime, dependency, data, and permission requirements still apply.
The packaged adaptive image service abstains until CNN license review, quality qualification, and activation are completed separately. It is not a ready-to-run hosted detector.
The local OpenAI plugin is not a public ChatGPT directory listing. Provider authentication, hosting, and attachment handoff are separate deployment work.

workflows.title: Inspect before connecting an MCP client
workflows.description: After the isolated installation in the 30-minute path, install the optional MCP extra in that same environment. These commands exit after writing local discovery and sample files; they do not call a provider API or download a model.
workflows.expected: Inspect the returned IDs and review result. The guaranteed-tool filter narrows this discovery output, not the server's runtime surface or filesystem permissions.

workflows.title: Connect an authorized local client
workflows.description: Configure the client to launch one of these alternatives with the installed environment's executable and an explicitly chosen workspace. These are long-running stdio servers, not one-shot validation commands. Stop the server when the session ends.
workflows.expected: Use the full surface only when the broader tools are intended. The image-service alternative exposes only capabilities, asset upload, submission, status, and cancellation. Ask for capabilities first; never reinterpret abstention as successful inference.

prompts.prompt: Validate my existing detection predictions strictly with YOLOZU; report errors without repairing the input.
prompts.expected: Confirm the user-selected local input, inspect the installed schema, then use strict validation. Do not invent a path or enable repair.

prompts.prompt: Show me a local YOLOZU evaluation example without downloading model weights.
prompts.expected: Use the self-contained 30-minute path and its generated toy inputs; label the proof as synthetic, not model-quality evidence.

prompts.prompt: Show the YOLOZU image service capabilities without running inference.
prompts.expected: Use image_service_capabilities on the image-service connection. Do not upload an image or submit execution.

prompts.prompt: Use YOLOZU to select the best CNN and guarantee its accuracy on my images.
prompts.expected: Explain that this guarantee is unavailable and that the default adaptive service abstains. Do not activate a model or fabricate a quality result.

thirty_minute.title: Install the evaluation extra in an isolated environment
thirty_minute.expected: The active environment contains YOLOZU and pycocotools. For a candidate build, install the candidate wheel plus pycocotools instead; the remaining commands are unchanged and run outside the source checkout.

thirty_minute.title: Create every tutorial input locally
thirty_minute.expected: The proof writes reports/quickstart/proof/toy_dataset, known_predictions.json, eval_report.json, and proof_report.json without downloading a model or dataset.

thirty_minute.title: Check both interface boundaries explicitly
thirty_minute.expected: Both validators exit successfully. These paths are outputs of the preceding proof command, not repository fixtures or guessed user paths.

thirty_minute.title: Run real COCOeval with concise flags
thirty_minute.expected: eval_coco.json has status ok, dry_run false, validation mode strict, repair disabled, and real COCO metrics. Evaluation is strict by default.

thirty_minute.title: Inspect the real report
thirty_minute.expected: Confirm status ok, dry_run false, validation mode strict, repair disabled, the evaluated image/detection counts, and non-null COCO metrics.

thirty_minute.title: Read before comparing
thirty_minute.expected: Confirm task, dataset/split, prediction source, export settings, protocol identity, metric family, and any skipped lane before comparing two reports.

dry_run_fallback.title: Core-install fallback (not real evaluation)
dry_run_fallback.description: Use this only when pycocotools is intentionally unavailable. It performs strict validation and conversion, writes dry_run true, and leaves all metrics null; do not present it as evaluation evidence.

python_api.title: Use the same strict lane from Python
python_api.description: The stable yolozu.api surface returns typed results and machine-readable exceptions without launching a subprocess or changing the working directory.
python_api.example:
from pathlib import Path

from yolozu.api import evaluate_coco

workspace = Path.cwd().resolve()
result = evaluate_coco(
    dataset=workspace / "reports/quickstart/proof/toy_dataset",
    predictions=workspace / "reports/quickstart/proof/known_predictions.json",
    split="val2017",
)
print(result.to_dict()["metrics"])
python_api.expected: The call uses the inputs created by doctor --proof, validates strictly by default, and returns a CocoEvaluationResult. Pass dry_run=True only when metrics are intentionally unavailable.

glossary.definition: The stable wrapped predictions boundary that lets validation and evaluation stay independent of the training or inference framework.
A predictions payload with schema version, prediction entries, and metadata needed to interpret how the artifact was produced.
The recorded dataset, split, metric settings, thresholds, and other evaluation choices that determine whether reports are comparable.
Producer-side preprocessing and output settings recorded in meta.export_settings so prediction artifacts can be interpreted and compared.
Prediction validation and evaluation capabilities that form the product's supported core boundary.
An adapter, exporter, or external training handoff that emits the stable predictions interface contract without replacing it.
A qualification path for runtime or backend parity used after stable prediction evaluation is already working.
An opt-in experiment over a stable artifact whose output does not establish production readiness.
A path that did not execute because a capability, artifact, runtime, or prerequisite was unavailable; it is not a passing result.
A report whose task, data, protocol, predictions provenance, and metric semantics align with the report it is compared against.

failures.symptom: The yolozu command is not found
failures.check: Confirm which Python environment received the package, then run python3 -m yolozu --help from that same interpreter.
failures.next: Reinstall into the intended environment; do not switch runtimes silently.

failures.check: Read the errors and drift_hints in the doctor report. The proof is CPU-only and does not require a model download.
failures.next: Resolve the reported package, path, or write-permission problem, then rerun into a fresh proof directory.

failures.symptom: Predictions validation reports missing or migrated fields
failures.check: Run strict validation on the wrapped artifact and compare its schema version with the predictions schema.
failures.next: Fix the producer or use the documented migration path before scoring.

failures.symptom: Dataset validation cannot resolve the split
failures.check: Use the split recorded in the dataset/proof artifact instead of assuming train, val, or val2017.
failures.next: Correct the dataset manifest or command so image IDs and split identity agree.

failures.check: Compare task, dataset/split, prediction source, export settings, protocol identity, class mapping, thresholds, and skip reasons.
failures.next: Align the differing input or protocol field before attributing the difference to a model or runtime.

failures.symptom: A backend row is skipped or conditional
failures.check: Read the canonical support matrix and the report's explicit status/reason.
failures.next: Provide the required artifact/runtime or keep the lane skipped; never reinterpret it as successful parity.

failures.symptom: A Research run changes the result
failures.check: Verify that the stable baseline predictions and evaluation report are preserved and linked.
failures.next: Treat the delta as Research evidence until a fixed protocol, rollback review, and environment qualification support a stronger conclusion.

failures.symptom: The visible demo has no overlays
failures.check: Confirm the demo report and overlays directory under the exact run directory printed by the command.
failures.next: Rerun the instance-seg demo into a new run directory and inspect the reported output paths.

report_checklist: Skipped, conditional, or unsupported lanes kept explicit
Visible evidence linked where the task provides it
